newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Office okays online sport channel.
newsitem.headline: German Office okays online sport channel.

text.p: Germany's anti-trust watchdog has approved plans by media giant Bertelsmann AG and publishing house Axel Springer Verlag AG to set up a jointly-owned online sports channel, Bertelsmann said on Thursday.

The channel, called Sportkanal GmbH, is due to start within the next four months and will offer interactive sports information and programming on the Internet and for the German online service AOL, the joint venture of America Online, Bertelsmann and Springer.

It will offer content from Springer publications Bild, the mass daily newspaper which operates one of the most popular German sites on the World Wide Web -- http://www.bild.de --, Sport-Bild and TV and online programming from both companies.

Bertelsmann will integrate its involvement in Sportkanal with its Interactive Studios, an online content development project that it started this year to create programming for online services and the Web.

It was not immediately clear whether Sportkanal would have any access to hugely popular first division German soccer matches, which are broadcast live by Premiere, the pay TV company partly owned by Bertelsmann.
